decisive_items: a 10-year history of a right‐sided scalp mass that had been stable and nontender until it was excised
the lesion recurred, gradually enlarged, ulcerated, and bled easily
response.rationale: The 10-year stable, nontender scalp mass followed by recurrence after excision is the classic indolent course of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans; later ulceration, bleeding, lymphadenopathy, and vertebral metastases fit fibrosarcomatous transformation. Squamous cell carcinoma and angiosarcoma usually behave aggressively from the outset and would not start with a decade-long stable lesion.

rejected.why: A 10-year stable pre-excision lesion is incompatible with the usual rapidly progressive course of angiosarcoma.

Metastatic SCC can produce an ulcerated fungating scalp mass with nodal/spinal metastases, but it does not explain the long-standing stable lesion and post-excision recurrence pattern that typify DFSP.
